clue.text: Armoured protection for 9 a.m. lesson? It delivers the goods!

parts.note: the first class of the school day is the one at nine in the morning
mail is flexible armour of linked metal rings

explanation.surface: A knight wonders about wearing chain mail to an early school lesson, then a delivery arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads the pieces in the order MAIL then FIRST CLASS, but 'for' just links them; the answer puts the lesson first.
explanation.definitionFit: The top tier of the postal service carries letters and parcels, so it brings what is sent.

clue.text: Tree is missing from this estuary

parts.note: a fir is a coniferous tree

indicators.note: the word is is taken away from the word this, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A walker notices that a tree has gone from the riverside estuary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' looks like the verb of the sentence, but it is the piece removed, with 'missing from' as the deletion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish word for a wide sea inlet where a river meets the sea.

clue.text: Sailor nipped by colourful insect is slowing down

indicators.note: being nipped by something means being caught between its jaws, so the sailor sits inside the insect

parts.note: a red ant is an insect described by its colour
tar is an old word for a seaman

explanation.surface: A seaman bitten by a bright bug finds himself slowing down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with this quality delays or hinders a process, as a fire treatment does.

clue.text: Tall story? A good deal of rage, if narrator's dull about it

indicators.note: the narrator and dull words wrap around it, meaning the shortened rage word

parts.note: a teller is someone who narrates a story

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, dropping its final letter

parts.note: rave is a craze or fashion, a rage
stale means flat and uninteresting

explanation.surface: A storyteller is so boring that his listeners fly into a rage at his exaggerated yarn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A good deal of' trims the last letter from the rage word; 'about it' puts what remains just after the narrator's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An exaggerated or untrue story, of the kind once told by people back from far-off places.

clue.text: Greatly desire to dance-non-stop trip?

parts.note: to long is to yearn for something
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: Someone yearns to dance on a long flight without a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Read playfully, a long hop is a lengthy flight with no stop on the way.

clue.text: University official used ban indiscriminately

indicators.note: used without care or order, so the letters are scattered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A college administrator has been slapping on bans without discrimination.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy to a dean in a college or cathedral, a junior office holder.

Angered, losing head, and ready to fight

annotationWithheld.clue: Angered, losing head, and ready to fight

clue.text: Moon explorer showing unnatural alien

indicators.note: alien means foreign or strange, telling us the letters are made unfamiliar by rearranging

explanation.surface: A space traveller to the Moon behaves in a way that seems unnatural and extraterrestrial.
explanation.definitionFit: A coined word on the model of astronaut for someone who travels to the Moon.

clue.text: Power shifting coastline etc., involving time?

definitions.text: Power shifting coastline etc., involving time?

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the time letter is placed among the rearranged letters
the words are moved about so their letters change places

explanation.surface: Geological forces move coastlines and other features over long ages.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: 'shifting' scrambles the coastline words and 'involving' sets the time letter among them, after the power letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The geological theory that the Earth's crust moves in sections over ages, reshaping continents.

clue.text: Irish broadcaster returned in bad weather to prepare for new job

indicators.note: the turned broadcaster sits inside the weather word

parts.note: rain is a common kind of bad weather

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the broadcaster's letters are read backwards

parts.note: RTE is Ireland's national broadcasting company

explanation.surface: An Irish TV company comes back in a downpour to train for a new role.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn new skills so as to take up a different kind of work.

clue.text: Carrollian character presumably called Tom?

definitions.meaning: the leader of the crew in Lewis Carroll's The Hunting of the Snark
large bells are often named Tom (Great Tom in Oxford), so a man who is a bell would bear that name

explanation.definitionFit: Carroll's Snark hunt is led by the town crier figure, and big bells such as Oxford's Great Tom share the name.

clue.text: Heroin, bit of speed, weed -something added to punch?

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin

indicators.note: only a small piece of the word, its first letter, is taken

parts.note: to hoe is to weed the ground

explanation.surface: A drug-taker lists heroin, some speed and cannabis, then asks what goes into the punchbowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weed' looks like cannabis, keeping the drug theme, but it is the gardening verb HOE. A horseshoe hidden in a boxing glove is the classic way to add force to a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-shaped iron fitted to a hoof, legendary as a weight slipped into a boxer's glove.

clue.text: Member of royal family died in debacle, retreating

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the whole thing is read in reverse
the died letter is placed inside the defeat word

parts.note: a rout is a crushing defeat
D is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: A royal dies during a disastrous military withdrawal.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry VII, Henry VIII and Elizabeth I belonged to this English ruling house.

clue.text: Loud support for trains is fading

parts.note: F stands for forte, loud in music
a rail is the track a train runs on

explanation.surface: Noisy backing for the railways is waning.
explanation.definitionFit: Weak and declining in health or strength.

clue.text: Slang — fair to assume 'translated' — a curious language

indicators.note: translated means turned into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Informal speech can be assumed to be rendered into a strange tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: A mix of French and English, an odd hybrid way of speaking.

clue.text: Dish? Consumed everything, returning for a cigar

parts.note: a pan is a cooking dish
ate means consumed

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for everything is read backwards

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: After eating a whole dish, someone goes back for a smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, thin type of cigar.

clue.text: Knock Tibet's location, mostly about time in monastery there

parts.note: to lam is to beat or knock

indicators.note: the shortened continent goes around the time word
most of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: Tibet is in Asia
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A traveller knocks at a Tibetan monastery, briefly giving its location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there' points back to Tibet, so the definition is a monastery in Tibet; 'mostly' clips the continent, which 'about' wraps round the time word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Buddhist monastery of Tibetan lamas.

clue.text: Almost none for tea, sadly -when it was served?

indicators.note: sadly signals that the letters are in a sorry, disordered state
almost all of the word is kept, its final letter dropped

explanation.surface: Someone laments that hardly any was left for tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts NONE to NON; with FOR and TEA those letters rearrange. 'it' in the definition is the tea of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is traditionally taken in the later part of the day, between lunch and evening.

clue.text: Ready to take group of three around a Canadian province

parts.note: on can mean ready or prepared

indicators.note: the trio wraps around the letter a

parts.note: a trio is a group of three

explanation.surface: A trio prepares to tour a part of Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: The province containing Toronto and Ottawa.

clue.text: No fees to take care of fifty swellings

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to take care of something is to hold it, so the fees enclose fifty

parts.note: dues are fees paid
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: No charge is made for treating fifty lumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Small rounded lumps or growths on the body or a plant.

clue.text: Old airplane company's satisfied

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
met as in met the requirements

explanation.surface: An aircraft firm says it is satisfied.
explanation.walkthrough: The de Havilland Comet was the first commercial jet airliner, from the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: The early British jet airliner of that name.

clue.text: Range's internal passage having a million taking refuge

indicators.note: the letters take refuge inside, sheltered within the passage

parts.note: the gut is the passage through the body

explanation.surface: A million people shelter in a passage within a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: The full scale or spectrum of something, from one end to the other.

clue.text: Important businessman's second opening curtailed

parts.note: mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: curtailed means having its tail cut, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a gulf is a gap or opening

explanation.surface: An important executive's second business opening is cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A powerful magnate or tycoon.

clue.text: Rotten lousy diet, without interest

indicators.note: rotten means decayed or broken down, so the letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint about a dreadful poor diet that is utterly boring.
explanation.definitionFit: In a boring, dull way.

clue.text: Arab country farmers, nothing less

indicators.note: less means minus, so the letter is taken away

parts.note: yeomen were small landowning farmers
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Farmers in an Arab country have nothing left.
explanation.definitionFit: The nation at the southern tip of the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: Pointed article soldiers number from one of their number?

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the soldiers are taken away from the regular

parts.note: a regular is a professional soldier, one of the soldiers' number
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A pointed piece about a soldier's number, written by one of the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their' refers back to 'soldiers', the Royal Engineers, and 'from' signals their removal from a regular soldier; the surface's 'number' sounds military but is just N.
explanation.definitionFit: Having sharp corners or points.

clue.text: Allowed border to go round one part of Ireland

indicators.note: the two words go round the numeral, enclosing it

parts.note: let means allowed
I is the Roman numeral for one
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A border is allowed to be moved around one region of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A county in the north-west of the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Calm attitude is briefly shown by sprite being plagued with demons

parts.note: is shortened to its contraction, an apostrophe and s
an elf is a sprite
possession is being taken over by evil spirits

explanation.surface: A fairy is said to be tormented by devils.
explanation.definitionFit: Composure and control over one's feelings.
